look_here_first: Start with a flowering axis carrying flattened two-ranked PAIRS of oval spikelets on one-sided racemes, usually several branches on a mature head. A short pictured branch alone cannot settle P. pubiflorum; confirm mature spikelets roughly 2.7–3.2 mm and check upper glume fine pubescence. Photo shows green spikelets with nearby leaves, not measured pubescence.

crew_field_steps: Find the tight vertical double-row appearance of the green oval spikelets on the visible raceme.
Identify the green leafy blade beside the head; the photographed finger gives coarse scale but is not a millimeter ruler.
Seek complete mature panicle, glume surface hair and collar ligule photos before distinguishing Florida paspalum, dallisgrass or others.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole plant and seedhead showing number of racemes on one culm.
Face-on pairwise spikelet rows and an individual 2.7–3.2 mm spikelet.
Upper glume in sharp side light to document hair/vein structure.
Leaf collar membrane and leaf-base hairs, if any; compare P. floridanum.

comparisons.key_distinctions: P. pubiflorum in accepted treatments commonly has 2–5(-7) unilateral racemes, small to medium 2.7–3.2 mm spikelets with glumes glabrous or minutely pubescent. Florida paspalum usually carries larger rounder spikelets; dallisgrass has conspicuous silky marginal hairs on larger spikelets; thin paspalum's varieties can differ dramatically in foliage hairs and smaller spikelets. Without a true scale, don't force it.
